title: Subdomain takeover: `login-mediaspace.unrealengine.com` CNAMEs to a generic target nothing owns
vulnerability_information:
`login-mediaspace.unrealengine.com` is a DNS record under `unrealengine.com` that still CNAMEs to `azurewebsites.net`. That target
answers with no records, so the delegation
terminates in nothing and the record outlived whatever used to hold it.

## Evidence

```
$ dig +short login-mediaspace.unrealengine.com CNAME
azurewebsites.net

$ dig +noall +comments +answer azurewebsites.net A
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, ANSWER: 0

$ curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://login-mediaspace.unrealengine.com/
000        # Could not resolve host
```

`NOERROR` with `ANSWER: 0` is NODATA, not a dead zone: the provider's own SOA and NS records are served normally, and a control name under the same zone returns the same shape. What is missing is the backend, not the DNS.

## Why this is claimable

The target answers NODATA, so nothing claims it. Which party can register it depends on the
provider; the delegation itself is broken regardless, and a record pointing at a name nobody
controls is a takeover waiting for the first person to claim it.

## What I did not do

I did not register anything or publish anything, so nothing here has been claimed. The checks above are
`dig` and one GET. If you want the takeover demonstrated rather than described, say so and I will claim
the name on a benign page, send you the timestamped proof, and release it afterwards — inside a window
you choose.

## Remediation

Remove the `login-mediaspace.unrealengine.com` CNAME, or point it at a backend you control. Audit the zone for other records delegating to `azurewebsites.net`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `dig +short login-mediaspace.unrealengine.com CNAME` → `azurewebsites.net`.
2. Resolve the target → NODATA, so nothing claims the name.
3. Claim the target at generic and publish content.
4. `https://login-mediaspace.unrealengine.com/` then serves it.
